## Repairs verified

`notice_failure` maps delivery errors to fixed phrases without copying their requester, tombstone reason or diagnostic text. Marking-told and task failures likewise return static failure phrases. `notify_owned`, `tell_requester` and `told_value` carry those fixed causes; the NOT-told line still indicates failure and retry, not a success-shaped fallback (`http/requests.rs:457-525,563-566`). Both earlier attack sources, missing requester id and forged tombstone reason, therefore cannot reach that line through the diagnostic.

Background start/list/tail/kill titles use the existing capped fence, and output paths have a 300-character fence. Parent-visible tail output is fenced line by line; the owner intentionally retains its own raw output. The comparison uses the actual job owner and resolved caller, not a rendered-label comparison. Access permissions are unchanged.

`ReleaseTarget`, instance suffixes and delivered/refusal holding labels render their role, instance and seat. Invalid stored times become length labels. The already-released refusal now fences the recorded reason, and the not-owner seat renders. No raw fields replace the operational release keys.

`Address::parse` rejects both whitespace and control characters. Thus U+2028/U+2029 are also refused by the whitespace check, not incorrectly assumed to be `is_control()`. Plain state applies that same parser to legacy stored addresses before copying them into prose.

`is_plain_folder` permits only bounded ASCII `docs/plans/<entry>` tokens, with no additional slash, whitespace, quote or control. An unshowable sole plan folder produces a length-only note and no plan edit; multiple-plan notes render each folder. The actual folder producer still requires a numbered entry, so the broader display helper is not an alternate traversal/plan selector.

The CLI fences the drained-request `error`. Its separate raw `why` branch is the fixed `REQUESTER_TOOK_ROLE` producer value (`delivery/role_send.rs:986-1005`), not another unguarded delivery error.

## Retained qualifications

The request command guards still compare a rendered id with its raw value. The previously noted invalid-label fixed point can pass that comparison; this does not enforce the showable-id grammar exactly. It cannot inject framing, and the complete command argument remains POSIX-quoted. No new security exploit is claimed.

`shown_time` borrows a raw string after a parser that trims whitespace, checking control characters but not all Unicode whitespace itself. A manually altered legacy timestamp surrounded by U+2028/U+2029 can therefore retain separators. Ordinary lineage writes parse and canonically `stamp` the time (`http/directory.rs:1353-1398`); no new ordinary-caller forged-instruction path was established. This is not universal single-line containment of arbitrary stored timestamps.

These fences contain structure, not semantic prompt-injection or arbitrary database tampering. Retained raw JSON is model-facing untrusted data. The SDK-origin state-error construction was not verified, so the inventory's all-errors trust claim is not broadened.

The not-owner refusal's seat and the multiple-folder note share inspected rendering helpers but lack separate targeted tests. This review does not regrade independent F135/F141 or #183 issuer/rotation work.
